chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'A man had me witness a testimony, and I recognize my handwriting and my seal, but I do not remember anything from the remainder, neither little nor much.'
He (the narrator) said: So he said to me: 'If your companion was trustworthy and there is with you a trustworthy man, then testify for him.'

key_terms.الشَّهَادَة: Testimony, witnessing — both the act of giving testimony in court and the document or event being witnessed
key_terms.الْخَاتَم: Seal, signet — a personal stamp used to authenticate documents in classical Islamic practice
key_terms.الْخَطّ: Handwriting, script — used here to identify one's own written attestation on a document
key_terms.ثِقَة: Trustworthy, reliable — a technical term in hadith and legal studies ('ilm al-rijal) for a narrator or witness whose reliability is established

ai.seo_question: Can a witness testify if he forgets the details but recognizes his handwriting and seal according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: The narrator 'Umar ibn Yazid posed to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) a practical legal question about testimony: he had previously witnessed a document but could no longer recall its details, only recognizing his own handwriting and seal. The Imam ruled that under such circumstances, if both the original party and a corroborating witness present are trustworthy (thiqa), the witnessing obligation may be fulfilled. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the reliability of witnesses — established through their known character ('adalah) — can supplement incomplete memory in legal testimony, a significant accommodation for practical court proceedings.
